title: quote_attribution_v1
description: A quotation put in the mouth of a real person is a different research question from a fact about them. It has an earliest documented source or it does not, and misattribution is common enough that a separate schema pays for itself.

quote_documented.description: Whether any contemporaneous record shows the purported speaker saying this.

context.description: Where and to whom it was said. A private remark and a public speech carry different clearance implications.

exact_wording.description: The wording of record, which is frequently not the wording in circulation.

commonly_misattributed.description: Whether this quotation is widely attributed to someone who did not say it.

actual_originator.description: Who said it, where the attribution is wrong.

paraphrase_distance.description: How far the script line sits from the documented wording. Invented dialogue attributed to a named living person is a clearance issue even when the sentiment is accurate.
